lastCompletedStory.title: Thread resolved backend into readPhaseModel at every dispatch site

nextStoryContext: All 6 named dispatch sites now thread the already-resolved backend local into readPhaseModel(phase, configPath?, backend): review.ts (reviewBackend), loop.ts (implBackend), plan-runner.ts's resolveAndSpawnPlanner/resolveAndSpawnAuditor (backend), commands/config.ts's printConfigShow (per-phase backend inside the ORDERED_PHASES.map), and commands/run.ts's orchestrator site (orchBackend, still resolved via the global readBackend() per the CAM-350 US-003 decision, only the ORDER changed so it feeds readPhaseModel). No new backend reads were added; each site just reordered its 2 existing resolution lines (backend first, then model) and passed the local through. scripts/cam/project.toml is untouched (all phases stay claude), confirmed via git diff --exit-code. file-size-budget.json ceilings raised for the 4 files whose comment additions pushed them over budget (run.ts, loop.ts, plan-runner.ts, review.ts), each by exactly the same +3/+4 lines the new backend-first comment blocks added; config.ts and run.ts's second edit fit under existing ceilings. This closes out the CAM-356 epic's call-site wiring (US-001 made the reader capable, US-002 wired every caller) -- a future story would only be needed if a 7th dispatch site is added later, or if the orchestrator's backend ever needs to become per-phase (currently deliberately global, CAM-350).

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure internal wiring of readPhaseModel/readPhaseBackend call-site ordering; no external library API surface was exercised (Bun.TOML behavior was already validated in the US-001 handoff for this same PRD).
